item.title: Torrential Rain Brings Deadly Floods Back to East Coast of Spain
item.description: Torrential rain lashed the east coast of Spain, flooding roads and leaving at least one person dead. The heavy rainfall started Wednesday in Valencia and Catalonia, reviving fears of a repeat of the devastating floods that killed more than 200 people in 2024. At the end of October 2024, an intense “dana” storm — a common phenomenon in Spain at the time of year — devastated the Valencia region.

item.title: China Construction Bank manager pleads guilty to accepting bribes from Vesttoo employee
item.description: In a turn of events, the first criminal charges related to the reinsurance letters of credit fraud have finally been confirmed, as a former China Construction Bank employee has pleaded guilty to accepting bribes to authenticate false collateral documentation. Back in June 2025 a Hong Kong bribery case took aim at the former China Construction Bank relationship manager , when the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region charged him with “allegedly conspiring with an employee of a fintech company to use various false standby letters of credit (L/Cs) and collateral letters,” that fintech being Vesttoo. The ICAC stated, “Lam Chun-yin, 32, former relationship manager of China Construction Bank (Asia) Corporation Limited (CCB (Asia)), pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy for an agent to accept advantages, contrary to section 9(1)(a) of the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance and section 159A of the Crimes Ordinance.

item.title: ExxonMobil Wins Approval for Texas Carbon Capture in 2-to-1 Vote
item.description: won approval for its Rose carbon-capture project in Texas, allowing the company to move ahead with the emission-reducing development that could be among the biggest of its kind. The Railroad Commission of Texas, the state’s primary oil and natural gas regulator, approved a permit to inject carbon dioxide underground with two commissioners voting in support and one against, according to a statement release by dissenting member Wayne Christian. The permit allows ExxonMobil to inject as much as 53 million tons of carbon dioxide over a 13-year period from industrial emitters along the Gulf Coast into rock strata about one mile (1.6 kilometers) underground for permanent storage.

item.title: 100 Years After Miami Hurricane, Similar Storm Would Top $200B in Losses—Swiss Re
item.description: “That lesson extends well beyond Florida: As populations and asset values increase in areas exposed to natural catastrophes, so does the potential for large insured losses.” And 34 years after Hurricane Andrew made landfall near Miami and changed building codes and construction practices in the state, a similar storm would produce almost $100 billion in insured losses, Swiss Re estimated. If the storm were to develop into a Category 5 hurricane that strikes heavily populated cities like Miami or Tampa Bay, the insured losses could top $300 billion—more than any previous insured-loss event, Swiss Re said in a report released this week. “One hundred years after the Great Miami Hurricane, the question is not simply how powerful the next major hurricane will be, but what it will encounter when it reaches shore,” Balz Grollimund, head of catastrophe perils at Swiss Re said in the report this week.

item.title: Chubb names new digital business leaders
item.description: Chubb has appointed Johan Oosthuizen global head of digital business, giving him responsibility for the insurer’s digital operations, including partnership acquisition and performance and product deployment. Lazaro joined Chubb in 2016 as head of digital for Latin America and most recently served as head of digital business for Overseas General Insurance. item.title: Hershey Defeats Reese’s Lawsuit Over Halloween Pumpkins That Lacked ‘Cool’ Carvings
item.description: Hershey won the dismissal of a lawsuit claiming it let down consumers because its Halloween-themed Reese’s pumpkins lacked the decorative carved designs shown on the packaging. “Plaintiffs do not allege that the Hershey’s Reese’s Peanut Butter Pumpkins that they purchased were defective or worthless or that they lost all economic value because of the absence of the decorative carvings.” The judge also said Vidal and Granados could not show they paid up to 25% too much by citing Reese’s prices at Target, at Walmart and in Hershey’s online store, because they bought their candy at a Publix supermarket. In a court filing seeking the lawsuit’s dismissal, Hershey said its packaging included a disclaimer that the depicted carvings were a “decorating suggestion.”

item.title: White House Weighs US Incubator for Cyber Research, Startups
item.description: The White House’s Office of the National Cyber Director has been drafting an executive order that would establish a program to research and develop cyber technologies that are aligned with the priorities of the U.S. The Trump administration is weighing a plan to establish a government-led incubator aimed at investing in cybersecurity research and spinning out startups focused on developing tools for the government to use, according to people familiar with the situation. government, the effort has been compared with the way Israel closely aligns its military priorities with the focus of cybersecurity startups, venture capital investments and academic research in the country, according to the people familiar with the plans.

item.title: Satellites Show Earth Lost More Than 12T Tons of Ice in 47 Years
item.description: About 12.5 trillion tons (11.3 trillion metric tons) of ice from glaciers in Greenland and Antarctica have melted since 1979, which is enough frozen water to stack ice 5 feet (1.5 meters) deep across the continental United States, according to a major scientific report. A warming Earth is accelerating the melting of the planet’s two major ice sheets, with five-sixths of the melt not coming from hotter air, but from warmer waters eating away at the ice sheets from below and the sides, with glaciers flowing into the oceans, according to a study in Wednesday’s journal Scientific Data. But by incorporating NASA satellites, the scientists were able to chart ice sheet volumes in Antarctica back to 1979 and in Greenland back to 1972.

item.title: UK Insurers Urge Bank of England to Rethink ‘Dynamic’ Stress Test
item.description: Britain’s insurance industry is urging the Bank of England’s regulatory arm to rethink its live crisis simulation, citing heavy reporting demands and unrealistic scenarios in a stress test that pushed firms “to their absolute limit.” The Prudential Regulation Authority’s first “dynamic” stress test, which ran over three weeks in May, subjected insurers to successive crises including a U.S. Unlike previous stress tests that assessed how insurers would handle predefined shocks, this one – known as DyGIST – tested insurers’ ability to respond in real time to adverse conditions as they unfold, with scenario details revealed only during the live exercise. “The accumulation of scenarios in such a short time frame was very unlikely,” said Nafisah Hussain, director of public policy at the International Underwriting Association, a trade body for insurers and reinsurers in the London market that has fed its views back to the PRA.

item.title: Busy August pushes Allstate’s current aggregate year pre-tax cat losses to $3.15bn
item.description: A busy August in catastrophe loss terms from severe weather activity has resulted in large US insurer Allstate reporting $748 million in pre-tax losses, which has lifted the total across the current annual aggregate risk period for its catastrophe bonds to $3.15 billion so far. July and August were particularly busy months in catastrophe loss terms for Allstate, with the two-month period generating a combined $1.43 billion in pre-tax losses, or $1.13 billion, after-tax Allstate currently has annual aggregate protection from only one cat bond tranche, the $150 million Class B tranche of notes issued through its Sanders Re III Ltd. item.title: Sompo International hires Nicolas Berg to head UK Insurance business
item.description: Sompo International has appointed Nicolas (Nic) Berg as chief executive officer of its UK Insurance business, succeeding Sarah Stanford, who is stepping down after leading the business through the initial integration period following Sompo’s acquisition of Aspen. item.title: Jensten Group to acquire technology-focused corporate broker Venture Risks Group
item.description: Jensten Group has agreed to acquire Venture Risks Group (VRG), a specialist technology-focused corporate broker, as it looks to expand its presence in the technology and life sciences sectors. The transaction, which is expected to complete in October 2026, will further strengthen Jensten Group’s technology, media, cyber, and life sciences division. It will also enhance the group’s specialist capabilities across professional indemnity, cyber, and technology-related risks.

item.title: Earnix pushes insurance AI from advice into action with Agent Hub launch
item.description: Earnix, a Boston-headquartered insurtech, has launched Agent Hub, bringing more than 25 insurance-specific AI agents and apps into its AI Orchestration System (AIOS). The new catalogue brings agentic AI directly into Earnix’s pricing and rating, underwriting, and customer engagement solutions. As AI increases the speed and scope of what insurers can analyse and recommend, Earnix argues that the next step is enabling intelligence to operate within the business processes where those decisions are made, while maintaining the governance and accountability required for high-stakes insurance activity.

item.title: Edmond de Rothschild Says Client Queries ‘Pouring in’ After Europe’s Wildfires
item.description: Edmond de Rothschild Group, the Swiss money manager, says it’s been fielding client inquiries since the summer amid concerns that Europe’s intensifying wildfire season represents a fundamental shift in how to view portfolio risk in the region. “Since our clientele is very European, questions have really been pouring in much more frequently since this summer — far more so than during the massive wildfires in Los Angeles.” De Tessieres says EdR now intends to conduct “more frequent portfolio valuations” to identify which holdings are most exposed. For example, one Europe-focused client “asked very specifically whether this has an impact on the valuations of her real estate portfolio, particularly on specific properties within her portfolio,” de Tessieres said in an interview.

item.title: Zillow Loses Antitrust Battle Over Chicago Area Listing Feed
item.description: Seattle-based Zillow previously won a court order that reinstated the Chicago-area listings after MRED cut off its data feed in May. in Chicago dissolved a previous order that required Midwest Real Estate Data, the multiple listings service for the Chicagoland area, to temporarily maintain Zillow’s access to listings. “If Zillow doesn’t enforce its listing ban, it will not lose access to the listing feeds and it can avoid any harm.” MRED said the decision reinforces the ability of listing services “to consistently enforce their rules and data licensing agreements.” In a statement on its website, Zillow said it was disappointed in the decision, which it called “a step back for Chicago home buyers and sellers.” The company said it will continue with the case as it moves into arbitration.

item.title: The Importance of Source Traceability in AI Medical Chronologies: Why Every Entry Must Cite Its Source
item.description: Source traceability in a medical chronology means every individual entry carries a citation: the name of the source document, the provider or facility, the date of service, and the specific page in the original record the entry was drawn from. It’s important to know whether every entry in the generated AI medical chronology can be traced back to a specific document, provider, date, and page in the original record set. item.title: FCA sets out steps to support small businesses' access to finance
item.description: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) could access finance more easily after the FCA sets out practical steps to help. As part of its commitment to supporting growth, the FCA is focusing its next steps in three areas to help reduce friction: Graeme Reynolds, FCA director of competition, said: 'Small businesses need to be able to access the finance they need at the right time to start up, grow and invest. item.title: Property reinsurance investing offers more manageable tail risk than perceived: Agecroft
item.description: Amongst the primary benefits, Steinbrugge highlights how property reinsurance investments can offer a more attractive and manageable tail-risk profile than commonly perceived. While property reinsurance and insurance-linked investment strategies are often viewed as carrying significant tail risk, Agecroft Partners believes that carefully constructed portfolios and disciplined underwriting can help to manage downside volatility more effectively than headline risk profiles may suggest. Steinbrugge further added: “While property reinsurance is often viewed as carrying significant tail risk, carefully constructed portfolios and disciplined underwriting can potentially manage downside volatility more effectively than the headline risk profile might suggest.” In addition, the CEO affirms that property reinsurance can also offer modeled forward returns that outperform many traditional fixed-income strategies.

item.title: Climate, Seismic Factors Primed ‘Unprecedented’ Nepal Disaster
item.description: The catastrophic mountain flooding in Nepal that killed more than 1,300 people was driven by a complex web of climate and seismic processes that made it nearly impossible to predict, according to an international team of scientists. “This is an unprecedented disaster in the Himalayas,” said Walter Immerzeel, a mountain hydrologist at Utrecht University and co-author of the report, during a press briefing. Nepal has already sought compensation from the United Nations Fund for responding to Loss and Damage, a nascent climate-aid system set up to help developing nations deal with the worst impacts of global warming.

item.title: El Niño, War Raise Asia’s Food Security Risks, Verisk Maplecroft Says
item.description: Severe weather disruptions will amplify food security risks in Asia, potentially triggering civil unrest and political instability in vulnerable countries such as India, Indonesia and the Philippines, according to consultancy Verisk Maplecroft. Over half of countries that are at high- or very high-risk on Verisk Maplecroft’s Food Security Index also sit within the two highest categories of its predictive Civil Unrest Index. For conflict-stricken nations like Afghanistan and Myanmar, a food shock would raise the risk of a humanitarian catastrophe, it added.

item.title: Russia’s Attacks on Europe Are Getting More Brazen and More Dangerous
item.description: “As a company whose systems are used by several NATO member states and other ally and partner nations, including Ukraine, we need to take the resultant risks into account.” Read more: Europe Struggles to Counter Russian Attacks Falling Short of War Just this week, the US Justice Department accused the Russian intelligence service of “conspiring to finance terrorism and commit murder for hire” in Europe at the behest of the Kremlin. item.title: Roost acquired; new owner discontinues Security360

item.title: Palette embeds fine-art transit insurance

item.title: Why Automation-First AI Falls Short in Specialty Lines
item.description: A system can identify every limit, exclusion and endorsement in a policy and still get the coverage analysis wrong. It may read every page yet miss how an endorsement changes the coverage grant, where an excess layer departs from the underlying coverage, or how the facts change a provision’s meaning. Coverage is a promise wrapped in documents.
